role: external oracle for the electric near field inside a patterned layer with a curved wall: 3D finite-element fields of a dielectric cylinder and of a metal one in the same cell, which the split reconstructions and the plain Fourier sum are measured against

references.build: FEniCS (dolfin) 2019.1 underneath, gmsh for the geometry and the mesh, MUMPS direct solve out of core

modified.description: used through its public Python API; the package itself was not changed

references.settings: Maxwell3DPeriodic on one eighth of the cell, using the exact mirror symmetries of normal incidence with E along x (the x mirror a perfect electric wall, the y mirror a perfect magnetic wall, and an even/odd split in z, two solves); second-order edge (Nedelec) elements; perfectly matched layers above and below. Dielectric run (E): relative residual of the two direct solves 3.0e-12 and 2.3e-12, R = 0.024309 and T = 0.975554 from the same solution. Metal run (E_metal): the same mesh, residuals 1.8e-12 and 1.4e-12, R = 0.187990 and T = 0.791543. The stored phasors are in gyptis's time convention, the conjugate of Wavebit's; the consumer maps them as -exp(2 pi i h / wavelength) * conj(E), with h the layer thickness
references.discretization: tetrahedral mesh graded toward the cylinder wall and its rims, 94078 cells and 621968 complex unknowns per solve, smallest edge 2.41 nm; the product side is a Fourier truncation of the same cell

generator.command: python fem_cyl.py c100_T4 c100 T4 12.25 1 for E; the same model with the cylinder at -20-1.5j (gyptis's convention) for E_metal, from a later revision of the script whose hash was not kept; then the plane samples laid out on the 48 x 48 grid

cost.note: both runs, two solves each, factorization out of core

cylinder_epsilon.E_metal: -20+1.5j in Wavebit's convention (loss is a positive imaginary part); the run takes its conjugate

cell.centre: the cylinder axis is the cell centre

samples.plane: mid-height of the layer, z = 75 nm above its lower face
samples.layout: E[j, i, component] and E_metal[j, i, component] at (x[i], y[j]), components (Ex, Ey, Ez)

outcomes.reference_self_check: the next coarser mesh level (53246 cells) differs from this one, over the same 2304 samples, by 0.11% of the plane RMS of the in-plane field for the dielectric cylinder (2.0% of it at the worst sample and component; R 0.024314 against 0.024309) and by 0.15% for the metal one (2.8% at the worst; R 0.188064 against 0.187990)
